description: Human-scored scenarios for adaptive planner/worker coordination, single-writer delegation, targeted review requests, findings iterations, and approval pauses.

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner and worker coordination sent messages without checking pending asks first and used ambiguous session-ID prefixes instead of retrieving exact IDs.
scenarios.intended_behavior: All roles call pending first before every outbound send or ask. If it reports an inbound ask, reply to that ask immediately without calling send, ask, list-cwd, or another pending first; only when it reports no inbound ask may the role immediately call list-cwd, then send or ask using the identifier token returned verbatim by that immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result (including an authoritative short ID); guessed, reconstructed, extended, further-abbreviated, stale, display-name, alias, and otherwise altered targets are forbidden.
scenarios.prompt: You are the planner or worker coordinating with a peer. Describe the Intercom check before a send or ask, and the immediate action when pending reports an inbound ask versus when it reports none, including how you retrieve the exact target.
must: Call Intercom pending first before every outbound send or ask
Reply immediately when pending reports an inbound ask
Do not call send, ask, list-cwd, or another pending before that reply
Immediately call list-cwd when pending reports no inbound ask
Use the identifier token returned verbatim by that immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result, including an authoritative short ID
avoid: Use reply without checking pending
Call pending again before replying to the inbound ask
Send without calling list-cwd again after no pending ask
Use a guessed, reconstructed, extended, further-abbreviated, stale, display-name, alias, or otherwise altered target

scenarios.observed_failure: A worker used a stale or altered session target, treated an undelivered Intercom message as sent, or continued after delivery failed.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Use the identifier token returned verbatim by the immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result (including its short ID), require successful delivery before treating a result or review request as sent, and recover one send failure by checking pending first; if it reports an inbound ask, reply immediately without calling send, ask, list-cwd, or another pending first; otherwise use a fresh list-cwd before retrying once or surfacing the unavailable planner as a blocker.
scenarios.prompt: Your Intercom send to the assigning planner reports delivery failure. Describe the target you may use, what you do when pending reports an inbound ask versus none, the checks and exactly one retry you perform, and whether you continue, commit, or close if the planner is no longer live.
must: Use only the identifier token returned verbatim by the immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result, including an authoritative short ID
Treat the result or review request as sent only after successful delivery
Do not call send or list-cwd when pending reports an inbound ask
Do not retry the stale target or continue, commit, or close after delivery failure
Call pending first after the failed send
Use reply immediately and do not call send, ask, list-cwd, or another pending before replying when pending reports an inbound ask
Otherwise call a fresh list-cwd before retrying
Retry exactly once only if the intended planner remains live; otherwise pause and surface the unavailable planner as a blocker
avoid: Use a display name, alias, or an altered session-ID token
Treat a failed send as delivered
Retry the stale target more than once
Continue implementation or mark the task complete while the planner is unavailable

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner sessions performed delegated implementation work or required rigid protocol fields instead of coordinating one writer.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner sends a bounded natural-language task to one same-directory worker and retains review ownership without editing.
scenarios.prompt: A same-directory worker is available. The requested feature requires repository edits and tests. Describe your next coordination steps, including whether you edit files yourself and what you send to the worker.
must: Use Intercom send for a concise natural-language task with goal, scope or invariants, and checks
Leave implementation edits and tests to the sole-writer worker
Plan to review the actual diff and verification
avoid: Perform the delegated implementation
Require B_AGENTIC_TASK fields
Ask the user to relay the task

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner handed off before finishing discovery, then continued exploring and issued new implementation requests while the worker edited, causing scope drift.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner finishes discovery and settles one bounded approach before handoff; the handoff names expected paths/symbols, scope/non-goals, invariants, and checks. While the worker edits, planner work is limited to independent read-only work outside that set; it does not mutate, revise in-flight scope, issue another implementation request, or review the in-flight diff before the worker's terminal result. After the result, the planner re-reads actual changed paths before review.
scenarios.prompt: A same-directory worker is available for a feature that needs repository exploration before implementation. Describe how you sequence discovery, the expected paths/symbols in the handoff, any approach agreement, independent work while editing, and review after the worker's terminal result.
must: Finish the necessary discovery and settle the approach before one bounded handoff
Name expected paths/symbols, scope/non-goals, invariants, and checks in the handoff
If needed, agree with the worker on the final approach before edits begin
While the worker edits, do only independent read-only work outside the expected set
Do not mutate, revise in-flight scope, issue another implementation request, or review the in-flight diff before the terminal result
Re-read actual changed paths before review after the terminal result
avoid: Send speculative follow-up implementation requests
Continue researching while the worker edits
Perform the implementation in the planner session

scenarios.observed_failure: The planner profile said external b-research was delegated with worker-owned skills and left pre-edit approach agreement and send-versus-ask responsibilities implicit, allowing research delegation or ask-based waiting.
scenarios.intended_behavior: External b-research remains planner-owned. When needed, the planner agrees with the worker on the approach before edits begin; send is for task delegation, terminal results, review requests/findings, and any question/request needing material work, while ask is only for one focused question whose answer needs no substantial investigation, implementation, or waiting—not for waiting on a delegated result.
scenarios.prompt: You are coordinating a task that needs external research and then worker edits. Explain who performs the research, when you agree on the approach, and whether you use send or ask for delegation, terminal results, review requests/findings, quick answers, material requests, and waiting.
must: Keep external b-research planner-owned rather than delegating it
Agree with the worker on the approach before edits begin when needed
Use send for task delegation, terminal results, review requests/findings, and any question/request needing material work
Use ask only for one focused question whose answer needs no substantial investigation, implementation, or waiting
Do not use ask to wait for a delegated result
avoid: Delegate external b-research as worker-owned
Start worker edits before needed approach agreement
Use ask for task delegation or result/review reporting
Use ask to wait for the delegated result

scenarios.observed_failure: Workers completed implementation but did not retain the assigning planner target or pause while review was pending.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The worker uses send for the result and review request to the assigning planner with evidence, then stops editing until findings or new work arrive.
scenarios.prompt: Planner session planner-7 assigned a clear implementation task. The implementation and useful verification are now complete. Describe the exact coordination action you take next and whether you continue editing afterward.
must: Send planner-7 the changed paths, verification outcomes, and remaining gaps
Pause all edits after the review request
Resume only for actionable findings or a new task
avoid: Send the result to an unspecified session
Continue editing while review is pending
Use ask for a non-blocking review request
Use ask to make the planner wait for the worker's delegated result

scenarios.observed_failure: A worker re-delegated assigned worker-owned implementation to another worker, creating a delegation loop instead of executing the bounded task.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The assigned worker executes worker-owned work itself and never hands it to another worker; it may ask the assigning planner only for blocker, scope, or external-research decisions.
scenarios.prompt: You are assigned a bounded worker-owned implementation task in a two-role session, and another worker is available. Describe who executes the task, whether you may hand it off, and which decisions you may ask the assigning planner to resolve.
must: Execute the assigned worker-owned work yourself as the sole worktree writer
Never delegate or hand off the assigned task to another worker
Ask the assigning planner only for a material blocker, scope decision, or external-research decision
avoid: Delegate the assigned task or any part of it to another worker
Use another worker to avoid executing the assigned work
Ask the user directly for a two-role blocker or scope decision

scenarios.observed_failure: A worker paused without reporting when no edits were needed or when the task ended with a gap, leaving the assigning planner without a terminal result.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Every terminal outcome for any assigned worker task—completed, no-change, blocked, or reported gap—is successfully sent to the same assigning planner before pausing, with evidence and remaining gaps under the five fixed headings Changed, Verification, Coverage, Deviations, and Gaps; worktree-changing results also ask the assigning planner to run actual b-review.
scenarios.prompt: Your assigned task completes, needs no edits, becomes blocked, or ends with a reported gap. Describe the terminal message you send, its target and contents, and whether you pause afterward.
must: For every assigned task, send a terminal completion/result to the same assigning planner before pausing
Use the five fixed headings Changed, Verification, Coverage, Deviations, and Gaps in every terminal report
Report the completed, no-change, blocked, or reported-gap outcome along with changed paths, acceptance coverage, exact checks, deviations, and gaps
Pause only after successful delivery rather than stopping silently
For a worktree-changing result, ask the assigning planner to run actual b-review and do not self-review
avoid: Stop without sending because no edits were needed
Omit the terminal result because a gap remains
Send the result to another worker or an unspecified session
Pause before successful delivery or treat an attempted send as delivered
Invoke, load, or execute b-review yourself

scenarios.observed_failure: Workers loaded or ran planner-owned b-review on their own worktree diff, mistaking a terminal review request for performing the review.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Worker mode never invokes, loads, or executes planner-owned b-review. For a worktree-changing result it successfully sends a terminal report/review request to the same assigning planner, asking that planner to run actual b-review, then pauses.
scenarios.prompt: You completed a worktree-changing task assigned by planner-7. Describe whether you load or run b-review yourself, the terminal report you send to planner-7, how you request actual review, and when you pause.
must: Never invoke, load, or execute planner-owned b-review yourself
Distinguish the terminal report/review request to the assigning planner from executing b-review
Successfully send planner-7 the terminal report under Changed, Verification, Coverage, Deviations, and Gaps
Ask planner-7 to run actual b-review against the approved baseline for the worktree-changing result
Pause after successful delivery and wait for findings or new work
avoid: Load or invoke b-review to inspect or approve your own diff
Treat a terminal report or review request as the b-review result
Pause before the terminal send is successfully delivered
Send the worktree result to another worker or an unspecified session

scenarios.observed_failure: A worker asked the user directly, stopped midway, or sent a premature completion/review message while the planner waited after encountering an unresolved issue or blocker.
scenarios.intended_behavior: For a quick two-role blocker or scope question, the worker calls pending first; it replies without list-cwd, send, or ask if an inbound ask exists, otherwise immediately refreshes list-cwd and uses ask to the assigning planner with one focused question targeted by that returned identifier token verbatim (including an authoritative short ID). A material blocker or request needing investigation uses send instead; neither action transfers the assigned task, and the worker keeps the task open while waiting.
scenarios.prompt: During a bounded implementation task, repository evidence leaves either a quick scope question or a material blocker. Describe which Intercom action you use for each, the pending-first target sequence, and whether you close, complete, or review the task while waiting.
must: Use ask only for a single focused question whose answer needs no substantial investigation, implementation, or waiting
After pending reports no inbound ask, immediately refresh list-cwd then use ask for the assigning planner with its returned identifier token verbatim, including an authoritative short ID
When pending reports an inbound ask, use reply and do not call list-cwd, send, or ask
Use send for a material blocker or request needing investigation, implementation, or waiting
Wait for the planner's response and keep the task open without sending a premature completion/review message
avoid: Ask the user directly
Send a completion or review request before the blocker is resolved
Stop midway without asking the planner

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner reviews identified defects but fixed them directly, creating concurrent writers.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner sends actionable findings to the worker and waits for a revised verified result.
scenarios.prompt: The worker requests review with changed paths and passing checks, but your diff review finds a concrete correctness bug. Describe what you do next and who edits the fix.
must: Send the actionable finding to the worker
Keep the worker as the sole worktree writer
Wait for a revised result and review again
avoid: Fix the bug in the planner session
Approve despite the correctness finding
Require a structured review schema

scenarios.observed_failure: Workers treated review findings as final approval or continued without re-verification and a new review request.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The worker applies findings, verifies, sends a revised result to the same planner, and pauses again until approval.
scenarios.prompt: The assigning planner returns one actionable correctness finding on your completed implementation. Describe the iteration through approval, including verification, messaging target, and editing pauses.
must: Apply the finding as the sole writer and verify the fix
Send the revised result to the assigning planner
Pause again and remain idle after approval
avoid: Treat findings as approval
Delegate the fix to another worker
Continue editing after requesting re-review

scenarios.observed_failure: Planners marked delegated tasks done, complete, approved, or closed before the actual b-review skill passed, or substituted a regular/generic review or bypassed the gate while inventing a decision from incomplete evidence.
scenarios.intended_behavior: Every delegated worktree-changing task stays open until the actual b-review skill passes against the actual diff and verification; a regular/generic review cannot substitute for it, and the planner resolves a worker's blocker via reply when possible or asks the user when scope and repository evidence cannot resolve it.
scenarios.prompt: The worker has sent an implementation with verification, but the actual b-review skill has not passed and a material decision cannot be resolved from the scope or repository evidence. Describe whether you mark the task done, complete, approved, or closed and what you send next.
must: Keep every delegated worktree-changing task open until the actual b-review skill has passed against the actual diff and verification
Treat a regular or generic review as insufficient
Never bypass the actual b-review gate
Escalate to the user rather than resolving by reply, because scope and repository evidence cannot resolve the decision
Ask the user one focused question when the blocker or decision cannot be resolved from scope or repository evidence
Keep the task open while waiting for the user's answer
Keep the worker as the sole worktree writer and use natural-language Intercom coordination
avoid: Mark the task done, complete, approved, or closed before actual b-review passes
Substitute a regular or generic review for b-review
Bypass the mandatory b-review gate
Invent a decision or close the task on unresolved ambiguity
Introduce a rigid protocol or state machine

scenarios.observed_failure: Planners repeatedly polled list-cwd or status after assigning work instead of waiting for the worker's result, adding coordination noise without improving readiness.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner checks pending first before every outbound send or ask; if it reports an inbound ask, the planner replies immediately without calling send, ask, list-cwd, or another pending first; otherwise it immediately calls list-cwd and sends or asks to the identifier token returned verbatim by that immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result (including an authoritative short ID), then waits for the worker's send result without further polling. Send is used for delegation, terminal results, review requests/findings, and material requests; ask is reserved for one focused quick-answer question.
scenarios.prompt: You are about to assign a bounded task to a ready same-directory worker. Describe the pending check, how you retrieve the exact target before sending, and what you do after the handoff while the worker edits, including whether you repeatedly call list-cwd or status and when ask is appropriate.
must: Reply immediately for an inbound ask without calling send, ask, list-cwd, or another pending
Immediately call list-cwd to retrieve the identifier token before a send or ask when no inbound ask is pending
Send or ask only to the identifier token returned verbatim by the immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd result, including an authoritative short ID
Wait for the worker's send result after the natural-language send handoff
Reserve ask for one focused quick-answer question whose answer needs no substantial investigation, implementation, or waiting
Use send for delegation, terminal results, review requests/findings, and any material request; do not poll while the worker edits
avoid: Repeatedly poll list-cwd or status after the exact-ID handoff
Invent a structured coordination state machine
Continue issuing implementation requests while the worker edits

scenarios.observed_failure: Planner sessions treated an implementation or fix request from the user as permission to edit, emit patches, or run modifying commands themselves.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner treats every implementation or fix request, including a direct user request, as work for the sole worker writer and delegates it or waits/provisions when no worker is ready.

Delegate to a ready worker or provision/wait when none is ready
Do not emit patches or modifying commands
avoid: Edit files in the planner session
Treat user wording as an exception to sole-worker ownership
Fall back to implementation when no worker is ready

scenarios.observed_failure: Ownership guidance could be misread as blocking planner access to worker skill text, or as allowing planner execution after inspecting it.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The planner may read any worker-owned SKILL.md for planning, delegation, audit, or review, but delegates its execution to a ready same-CWD worker. A new skill that performs browser verification is worker-owned under the classification criterion; unknown ownership also defaults to worker ownership.

Delegate b-implement execution to the ready same-CWD worker
Classify the new browser-verification skill as worker-owned because it requires worker capabilities
Treat an unrecognized or ambiguous skill as worker-owned
Do not implement when the worker is unavailable
avoid: Block reading b-implement solely because it is worker-owned
Execute b-implement in the planner session

scenarios.observed_failure: Workers rejected the short ID shown by list-cwd or reconstructed it into a longer target.
scenarios.intended_behavior: The exact short identifier token shown by the immediately preceding authoritative list-cwd output is a valid target; only altered or stale targets are forbidden.

scenarios.observed_failure: Delegated work lacked execution context and reviews could not connect findings to the approved work.
scenarios.intended_behavior: A non-trivial handoff, worker result, and actual review carry enough natural-language evidence to execute, review, and correct without a rigid schema.

Require actual b-review only because the delegated task changes the worktree
avoid: Require parsed protocol fields
Approve a generic review
Run planner-side tests instead of requesting bounded worker evidence

scenarios.intended_behavior: Every b-review response ends with exactly one standalone final line in one exact form: Verdict: READY FOR PR, Verdict: READY WITH FOLLOW-UPS, or Verdict: NEEDS FIXES; the final line has no Markdown decoration and no additional text follows it.
